title: First-order asymptotic expansion of a simple real transmission eigenvalue of a periodic scatterer of bounded support
author: Fioralba Cakoni and Shari Moskow
work: Asymptotic expansions for the transmission eigenvalues of periodic scatterers of bounded support
difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the article's own deduction of its main theorem - the first-order asymptotic expansion of a simple real transmission eigenvalue of a periodically oscillating scatterer of bounded support - from the Osborn-type nonlinear eigenvalue perturbation theorem that the article states as Theorem 1 and from the fourth-order homogenization estimates it proves. Even with the whole preceding apparatus available in the delivered context (the variational fourth-order reformulation of the interior transmission eigenvalue problem, the two-scale asymptotics with the cell problems for chi, gamma, alpha and B, the boundary correctors theta_eps^{(n)}, Lemma 2 on their L^2 boundedness, Propositions 1-2 and Corollary 2 giving the O(eps) operator estimate, Theorem 1 quoted from Osborn's theory, and the computed denominator (81) and numerator (82)), the counted proof is a source-local research argument rather than a qualification exercise: one must pass from the L^2 estimate of (T_eps(tau)-T_0(tau))f by C_tau eps to strong pointwise convergence of the operators uniformly on bounded regions of the complex plane, using the explicit coercivity of the fourth-order operator to make the constant tau-independent; one must establish collective compactness of the family T_eps(tau) from the uniform H^2 bound on u_eps = T_eps(tau)f; one must recognise that the hypotheses of the quoted perturbation theorem are met and that, because the eigenspace R(E) is one-dimensional here, the remainder on the right-hand side of its expansion is O(eps^2); and one must insert the article's own denominator (81) and numerator (82) into that expansion to obtain the explicit correction formula, in which the leading microstructure effect is the fourth-order boundary corrector theta_eps^{(2)} integrated against the scaled eigenfunction, under the explicit solvability condition that L^{-1}_{tau_0,0} phi paired with phi differs from (nbar-3)/(2 tau_0 nbar). Identifying that the boundary corrector, and not the bulk corrector, dominates the correction, and assembling the hypothesis chain (sign-definite contrast, simple homogenized eigenvalue, H^5 regularity of the eigenfunction) is research-level homogenization reasoning beyond ordinary PhD qualification problems in analysis.
